newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks seen back on record path.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks seen back on record path.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are poised to break new records in the week ahead, following on from a record closing high last week for the Hang Seng as investors remain comfortable with the interest rate outlook, analysts said.
U.S. economic data released on Friday reaffirmed moderating economic growth and analysts said the U.S. Federal Reserve was unlikely to raise interest rates in the near term.

"The market is likely to challenge its recent record intra-day high. The price level is not too far away from 13,000 (points). That is the consensus target now," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
Hong Kong's blue chip Hang Seng index scored a record closing high on Friday, rising 51.71 points to 12,529.27. Over last week, the index gained 140.89 points, or 1,14 percent.
The Hang Seng's record intra-day high stands at 12,602.34 points, reached on October 16.
China Everbright Research said in its weekly commentary it expected the Hang Seng index to break through resistance at 12,600 points and trade in a range of 12,400 to 12,700 points.

"Data showing that U.S. economic growth was slowing gave stocks a boost, taking pressure off the Fed to raise interest rates at the coming FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting mid-November," it said.
The U.S. Labour Department said on Friday that U.S. October non-farm payrolls rose 210,000, in line with forecasts, and average earnings per hour was unchanged.
Analysts said although they expected the Hang Seng to test higher levels in the upcoming week, there could be some profit-taking after the November 5 U.S. presidential election.
Analysts said there were worries of a Democratic sweep of the Congressional races.

"Disappointment with the U.S. election could cause the market to test 12,200 (points)," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities. He said investors were looking for "a balance of power".
Nervousness ahead of Election Day caused the Dow industrials to ease 7.45 points to 6,021.93 on Friday, after rising earlier on the back of the friendly economic data.

Analysts said local market action in the week ahead was likely to be livened up by the trading debuts of Concord Land Development Co Ltd, China Resources Beijing Land Ltd and Arts Optical International Holdings Ltd.
Shares in Concord Land, the property arm of Pacific Concord Holdings Ltd, are due to begin trading on Thursday.

China Resources Beijing Land, the China property unit of China Resources Enterprise Ltd, and Arts Optical are due to begin trading on Friday. Analysts expected an enthusiastic reponse to both Beijing Land and Arts Optical.
China Light and Power Co Ltd is due to release its final earnings on Monday and Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd is due to release interim results on Tuesday.
New World Development Co Ltd is scheduled to release full year earnings on Thursday.
